締.meaning: The <part>emperor</part> has eaten too many dumplings and his robe won't close. Six servants wind <part>thread</part> round and round his belly, leaning back with all their weight, until the buttons stop popping. Every morning they have to <kanji>tighten</kanji> it a little more.
締.on: When the thread runs out, they finish the job with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
締.kun: A <sound>shee</sound>p in the corner bleats for its <sound>Ma</sound> as the palace doors slam shut.

互.meaning: <part>Two</part> neighbours own a single clothes <part>iron</part> and pass it back and forth over the fence: today you press my shirts, tomorrow I press yours. Neither has bought one in twenty years. Everything between them is done <kanji>mutually</kanji>.
互.on: Whoever's turn it is wears swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles against the steam.
互.kun: One irons out the other's <sound>ta</sound>co stain; the other returns the favour with a <sound>ga</sound>rlic one.

仮.meaning: A hotel lobby boasts a gleaming <part>coat hook</part> under a sign: '<part>anti</part>-theft, guaranteed'. You hang up your coat, and the whole hook flops over: it's painted cardboard. The guarantee is a <kanji>sham</kanji>.
仮.on: Even the <sound>ca</sound>rp in the lobby pond is cardboard, propped up on a stick.
仮.kun: 'Stay <sound>ca</sound>lm,' says the manager, 'it's just for now,' and props a cardboard <sound>ree</sound>f in the pool.

担.meaning: At <part>daybreak</part> a tiny sailor hauls the ship's <part>anchor</part> out of the sea, heaves it onto his back and trudges inland, sweating. Nobody asked him to; he just thinks someone should carry it. He spends all day <kanji>shouldering</kanji> it.
担.on: His route takes him through a long dark <sound>tun</sound>nel, the anchor scraping sparks off the roof.
担.kun: For lunch he balances a plate of chicken <sound>katsu</sound> on top of the anchor.

評.meaning: A pancake judge stands on a chair and gives a long <part>speech</part> about every entry. Fluffy ones get a cheer, but any pancake <part>flat</part> as paper gets a frown and a low score. It's her job to <kanji>evaluate</kanji> them.
評.on: She taps one tall <sound>hee</sound>l as each plate comes up, and bops the flattest ones with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo.

順.meaning: A line of <part>rubber duck</part> toys floats down the <part>river</part>, nose to tail. When the front duck squeaks, all the rest turn left at once; two squeaks, and they spin. Not one ever swims its own way. They just <kanji>obey</kanji>.
順.on: They squeeze past a <sound>jun</sound>iper bush on the bank, one by one, never out of turn.

態.meaning: A bear with every <part>ability</part> under the sun can juggle, ski and bake, but its <part>heart</part> just isn't in it. It rolls its eyes, sighs loudly and lets the eggs drop on the floor. What a terrible <kanji>attitude</kanji>.
態.on: To look a bit more serious it puts on a <sound>tie</sound>, then chews the end of it.
態.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' wails the cook as it hurls an egg across the ba<sound>za</sound>ar and splats a <sound>to</sound>tem pole: on purpose.
